column1: What is AIT’s mission and vision?
column2:
The mission and vision of the Asian Institute of Technology (AIT) are as follows:

Mission
AIT's mission is to provide high-quality postgraduate education and research that is internationally recognized, innovative, and relevant to the needs of industry and society. It aims to contribute to sustainable development through education, research, and collaboration, with a focus on global challenges such as climate change, poverty, and inequality.

Vision
AIT's vision is to become a leading international research university that drives innovation and sustainability. It envisions a future where education and research are centered on solving global challenges, and where AIT plays a pivotal role in shaping a more equitable, sustainable, and resilient world.

Summary
Mission: Provide high-quality, internationally recognized postgraduate education and research that is innovative and relevant to industry and society, contributing to sustainable development.
Vision: To become a leading international research university that drives innovation and sustainability, addressing global challenges through education, research, and collaboration.
column4:

AIT's vision is **"Transforming AIT to be a respectable international graduate institution whose research and education contribute to the development of Asia, by making AIT more global, more innovative, more entrepreneurial, and more economically relevant—while leveraging on its social impact core strengths."**<cite doc="web_markdown.pdf" page="1"/>
## Mission
The mission is **"to develop highly qualified and committed professionals who will play a leading role in the sustainable development of the region and its integration into the global economy"**.<cite doc="web_markdown.pdf" page="1"/>

These guide AIT to become a trailblazer in advanced education, a leader in professional development programs, a hub for regional research projects, and a financially viable, self-sustaining institution with strong governance and leadership.<cite doc="web_markdown.pdf" page="1"/>

column1: What academic programs and fields of study are available at AIT?
column2:
AIT offers a variety of academic programs and fields of study, including:  

1. **Degree Programs**:  
   - **Master’s Programs**: 2-year Master’s (22–24 months) and 1-year Master’s/Professional Master’s/Diploma programs.  
   - **Doctoral Programs**: Minimum 42 months (7 semesters).  
   - **Unified Programs**: Combine undergraduate and graduate studies (e.g., final-year undergraduates start Master’s programs).  

2. **Specialized Fields**:  
   - **Agri-Business Management (ABM)**  
   - **Agricultural Systems And Engineering (ASE)**  
   - **Agricultural Systems, Engineering, and Agribusiness (ASEA)**  
   - **Professional Master’s Programs**: Banking & Finance, Business Analytics & Digital Transformation, Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG), Social Business and Entrepreneurship.  

3. **Non-Degree Programs**:  
   - Certificate programs, intensive English language courses, and training through the AIT Extension and Language Center.  

For detailed program specifics, visit [AIT’s Academic Programs page](https://ait.ac.th/academics/programs/).

column1: Does AIT offer academic exchange programs?
column2: Yes, AIT offers academic exchange programs with partner universities in Asia and Europe. These programs allow students to study abroad while earning credits toward their AIT degree. Scholarships are available to support outgoing exchange students, and applications can be submitted during the second semester of study at AIT. For more details, visit [AIT's International Exchange page](https://ait.ac.th/student/student-international-exchange/).

## Student International Exchange

AIT has partnerships with **around 60 international universities around the globe** for student exchange opportunities.<cite doc="web_markdown.pdf" page="203"/>

### **Key Details:**

**Objective:** To equip AIT students with balanced skills and knowledge by providing an opportunity to learn at a partner university abroad, cultivate academic knowledge, transversal skills, intercultural communication, and expand personal and professional networks.<cite doc="web_markdown.pdf" page="203"/>

**When to Apply:**<cite doc="web_markdown.pdf" page="203"/>
- **Spring Semester** (January to April): Application period is September 1-15
- **Fall Semester** (August to November): Application period is March 1-15

**Eligibility Requirements:**<cite doc="web_markdown.pdf" page="203"/>
- Must be enrolled in courses at AIT
- Must complete two semesters/four terms (for SOM) of coursework with **minimum CGPA of 3.0**
- **English level of at least 6.0** on AIT Standard
- Approval from Academic Advisor

**Credit Transfer:** The exchange period is equivalent to one semester and students need to complete **12 credits**, which can be done through:<cite doc="web_markdown.pdf" page="203"/>
- 12 credits of coursework transferred back to AIT, OR
- 9 credits of coursework + 3 credits of special study/AIT coursework, OR
- 6 credits of coursework + 6 credits of project/special study/AIT coursework

**Financial Support:** AIT Exchange Scholarships are available for outgoing exchange students thanks to donations from alumni and business partners.<cite doc="web_markdown.pdf" page="204"/>

AIT also accepts **incoming exchange students** from partner universities.<cite doc="web_markdown.pdf" page="209"/>

column1: Are AIT programs offered on a full-time or part-time basis?
column2: AIT offers both **full-time** and **part-time** (flexible) options for its programs. The **Flexible Master’s Option** is designed for working professionals and allows enrollment in courses (minimum 6 credits/2 courses per semester) without requiring full-time campus attendance. However, traditional full-time on-campus programs are also available. For detailed enrollment requirements, visit [AIT's admissions page](https://ait.ac.th/admissions/frequently-asked-questions/).

AIT programs are offered on **both full-time and part-time basis**, depending on the program type:

## **Traditional Programs - Full-Time**

Most AIT programs are designed as **full-time on-campus programs**, including:
- Regular Master's degrees (2 years)
- One-year Master's programs
- Doctoral programs
- MBA programs

## **Flexible Master's Option - Full-Time OR Part-Time**

For selected programs, AIT offers a **Flexible Master's Option** that allows you to choose:<cite doc="web_markdown.pdf" page="200"/>

**Full-Time:** 
- Graduate in **2 years** (minimum time)

**Part-Time:**
- Graduate within **4 years** (maximum study period)
- Requires a minimum of **2 courses per semester (6 credits)** and maximum of 15 credits<cite doc="web_markdown.pdf" page="200"/>

### **Key Point:**

"You do not need to prove that you are working to join the Flexible Master's Option. Actually, you can do the Flexible Master's Option full time and graduate in 2 years Or as a part-time student and graduate within 4 years. **It is totally up to your personal choice.**"<cite doc="web_markdown.pdf" page="200"/>

The Flexible Master's Option is particularly suitable for working professionals, as classes are delivered online via AIT's Hybrid Mode of Instruction, though students may still need to come to campus for certain activities such as labs and research work.<cite doc="web_markdown.pdf" page="200"/>

Note that the Flexible Master's Option is **only available for selected programs**, not all AIT programs.<cite doc="web_markdown.pdf" page="200"/>

column1: How long does it typically take to complete a Master’s program at AIT?
column2:
The typical duration to complete a Master’s program at AIT varies based on the program and study mode:  
- **Full-time (Flexible Master’s Option):** 2 academic years (22–24 months).  
- **Part-time (Flexible Master’s Option):** Up to 4 academic years.  

For standard full-time programs (e.g., MSc/MEng), the duration is generally **2 years**, while 1-year programs (e.g., MBA, Professional Master’s) exist but are shorter. The Flexible Master’s Option allows flexibility between 2 and 4 years.  

[Source](https://ait.ac.th/study/flexible-masters-option/)

column2:
To apply for a Master's program at Asian Institute of Technology (AIT), the requirements include:  

### **General Requirements**  
1. **Academic Qualification**:  
   - Hold a Bachelor’s degree (or equivalent) from a recognized institution in a relevant field.  
   - Minimum GPA: **2.75 or equivalent** at the undergraduate level.  

2. **English Proficiency**:  
   - **AIT-EET**: 6  
   - **IELTS**: Overall 6.0 (Writing 6.0)  
   - **TOEFL iBT**: Overall 80 (Writing 21–23)  
   - **PTE Academic**: Overall 52 (Writing 62–73)  

3. **Health and Conduct**:  
   - Be in satisfactory physical and mental health.  
   - Maintain a record of good conduct.  

---

### **Professional Master’s (PM) Program Requirements**  
In addition to the above, applicants must:  
- Have **at least 3 years of work experience** in areas related to the academic program.  
- Be **executives** in organizations/companies.  

---

### **Other Notes**  
- **Scholarship Eligibility**: Applicants in 1-year Master’s programs are **not eligible** for scholarships/fellowships.  
- **Flexible Master’s Option**: Allows part-time study (minimum 2 courses/semester, max 15 credits) with a maximum study period of **4 academic years**.  

For detailed application steps, visit [AIT’s Flexible Master’s page](https://ait.ac.th/study/flexible-phd-option/).  

**Source**: AIT official program descriptions and eligibility criteria.
column4:
Here are the **requirements to apply for a Master's degree at AIT:**

## **General Eligibility Requirements**

To be eligible for admission to a regular Master's program, you must:<cite doc="web_markdown.pdf" page="206"/>

### **1. Academic Qualifications**
- Hold a **Bachelor's degree** (normally from a four-year program), or its equivalent, in an appropriate field of study from an institution of good standing acceptable to AIT
- Have **undergraduate grades significantly above average**
- **Minimum CGPA requirement: 2.75 or equivalent** at the Bachelor's degree level

### **2. English Proficiency Requirement**

One of the following:<cite doc="web_markdown.pdf" page="206"/>
- **AIT-EET:** 6
- **IELTS Academic:** overall 6 (writing 6)
- **TOEFL iBT:** overall 80 (writing 21-23)
- **PTE Academic:** overall 52 (writing 62-73)

**Note:** Applicants applying for **full scholarships** must submit an English Proficiency Test Score of **6.0 (writing and overall)**.<cite doc="web_markdown.pdf" page="209"/>

### **3. Health and Conduct**
- Be in **satisfactory physical and mental health**
- Have a **record of good conduct**<cite doc="web_markdown.pdf" page="206"/>

## **Additional Requirements for Specific Programs**

### **Professional Master's (PM) Degree:**
In addition to the above requirements:<cite doc="web_markdown.pdf" page="206"/>
- Have at least **3 years of work experience** in areas related to the academic program at AIT
- Be **executives in organizations/companies**

### **MPhil Program (Research-focused 2-year program):**<cite doc="web_markdown.pdf" page="207"/>
- **Minimum CGPA: 3.0 out of 4.0** or equivalent at the Bachelor's degree level (higher than regular Master's)
- Submit a **brief outline of the research proposal**
- Same English proficiency requirements as regular Master's

## **Application Fees**

- **Application processing fee:** 25 USD or 800 Baht<cite doc="web_markdown.pdf" page="206"/>

## **Important Notes**

- **One program at a time:** An applicant can only apply for **one program at a time**<cite doc="web_markdown.pdf" page="206"/>
- **1-year Master's programs:** Applicants applying for 1-year Master Degree Programs are **not eligible for Scholarships/Fellowships**, though they may seek funding from external sponsors<cite doc="web_markdown.pdf" page="207"/>

## **English Proficiency Exemptions**

You may be exempted from English testing if:<cite doc="web_markdown.pdf" page="209"/>
- You are a **citizen of an English-speaking country** (Australia, Canada, Ireland, New Zealand, UK, USA) - proof of citizenship required
- You earned a degree at a university where **English is the sole medium of instruction** - requires a certificate signed by the University Registrar (subject to AIT's acceptance)

**January Semester/Term Intake:**

- July 25: for other applicants

**Application:** Complete your online application at the AIT admissions portal.<cite doc="web_markdown.pdf" page="206"/>

column1: What are the requirements to apply Phd in AIT?
column2:
To apply for a PhD at Asian Institute of Technology (AIT), the requirements include:  

1. **Academic Qualifications**:  
   - A four-year bachelor’s degree and a master’s degree (preferably with thesis work) from a recognized institution.  
   - Minimum CGPA of **3.5** at the master’s level (or equivalent). For applicants with a **one-year master’s degree**, additional coursework (12–24 credits) and a CGPA of 3.5 are required.

   - **AIT-EET**: 6  
   - **IELTS Academic**: Overall 6.0 (Writing 6.0)  
   - **TOEFL iBT**: Overall 80 (Writing 21–23)  
   - **PTE Academic**: Overall 52 (Writing 62–73)  

3. **Documents**:  
   - A **research proposal outline** (5–10 pages) detailing the dissertation topic and required facilities.  
   - **Two recommendation letters**.  

4. **Flexible PhD Option**:  
   - No campus attendance required for most coursework.  
   - Study at your own pace from any location.  

5. **Scholarships**:  
   - Eligible candidates may apply for AIT scholarships (details [here](https://ait.ac.th/financial/ait-scholarships/)).  

**Apply Here**: [AIT PhD Application Form](https://www.ait.ac.th/admissions/application-form/)

column1: What is the required IELTS or TOEFL score?
column2:
The required English proficiency scores for admission to Asian Institute of Technology (AIT) are as follows:  

- **IELTS-Academic Module**: A minimum score of **6.0** (with a **writing band of 6.0**).  
- **TOEFL**:  
  - **Paper Test (TOEFL PBT)**: 550 (writing score of 59–61).  
  - **Computer-Based Test (TOEFL CBT)**: 213 (writing score of 25–26).  
  - **Internet-Based Test (TOEFL IBT)**: 80 (writing score of 21–23).  

Alternatively, applicants can take the **AIT English Entry Test (AIT-EET)** and achieve a score of **6** (on a nine-point scale, similar to IELTS).  

For more details, refer to AIT’s [English Proficiency Requirements page](https://ait.ac.th/admissions/frequently-asked-questions/).

To determine whether you need to choose specific majors before applying, it depends on the program you're interested in. Here's a breakdown based on the provided information:

### 1. **For the Agricultural Systems Engineering and Agribusiness (ASEA) Program**  
   - **Preferred Majors**:  
     - **Agricultural Systems**: Relevant degrees include **Bachelor of Science in Agriculture**, **Biological Sciences**, **Engineering disciplines** (e.g., Electronics, Biotechnology, Mechanical Engineering), **Computer Science**, or **Food Science and Technology**.  
     - **Agribusiness Management**: Focuses on business and economics, so degrees in **Agricultural Economics**, **Business Administration**, or **Supply Chain Management** may be relevant.  
   - **Key Note**: While specific majors are preferred, the program emphasizes **relevance to the field** (e.g., agricultural systems, technology, or business) rather than strict major requirements.  

---

### 2. **For Other Programs (e.g., Engineering, Computer Science, etc.)**  
   - **Preferred Majors**:  
     - For **Master’s programs**, applicants typically need a **Bachelor’s degree in a relevant field** (e.g., Engineering, Computer Science, Biological Sciences, or related disciplines).  
     - For **Ph.D. programs**, a **Master’s degree in a related field** is usually required.  
   - **Key Note**: Specific majors are **preferred but not always mandatory**. The focus is on **academic background alignment** with the program’s research or curriculum focus (e.g., agriculture, technology, or business).  

---

### 3. **General Guidance**  
   - **Check Program-Specific Requirements**: Each program (e.g., ASEA, Engineering, or Computer Science) may have unique criteria. For example, the ASEA program explicitly lists acceptable undergraduate degrees.  
   - **GPA Requirements**: For Master’s programs, a minimum GPA of **2.75–3.5** (equivalent) is often required, but this varies by program.  
   - **Relevance Over Specificity**: While certain majors are highlighted, the admissions committee prioritizes **how your academic background aligns with the program’s goals** (e.g., agricultural systems, technology, or business).  

---

### Final Answer:  
You **do not need to pick a specific major** before applying, but your **academic background should align with the program’s focus areas**. For example:  
- For **agricultural programs**, degrees in **agriculture, engineering, or food science** are preferred.  
- For **technical programs**, **engineering, computer science, or related fields** are typically required.  

Always review the **specific program’s requirements** (e.g., ASEA’s listed degrees) for the most accurate guidance. If you’re unsure, contact the admissions office for clarification.

- MBA

- Agricultural Systems & Engineering
- Water Engineering and Management
- Environmental Engineering and Management
- Climate Change and Sustainable Development
- Gender and Development Studies
- etc.

## **Summary:**

Yes, you must choose a **specific program** before applying - you cannot apply generally to AIT or to multiple programs simultaneously. Choose carefully, as each application requires a separate fee and process.

column1: Do I need to apply for the scholarships listed on the AIT scholarship website?
column2:
No, you do not need to apply separately for financial aid (scholarships) at AIT. Source: [AIT Admissions FAQ](https://ait.ac.th/admissions/frequently-asked-questions/)

column1: Are scholarships available for both Master’s and PhD students?
column2:
Yes, scholarships are available for both Master’s and PhD students at Asian Institute of Technology (AIT). Here's a breakdown:

### **Master’s Scholarships**
1. **His Majesty the King’s Scholarships for Master’s Programs**  
   - Awarded to qualified candidates from Asian countries with excellent undergraduate academic records.  
   - Covers tuition, registration fees, accommodation, and a living allowance at AIT’s residential campus.  

2. **Her Majesty the Queen’s Scholarships for Master’s Programs**  
   - Open to Asian nationals pursuing their first Master’s degree in programs offered by the Faculty of Civil and Environmental Engineering (FCEE), Faculty of Advanced Science and Technology (FAST), or School of Management (SOM).  

3. **Research Fellow Program for Public Policy and Asian Study**  
   - Targets PhD students (though explicitly mentioned for PhDs, it may overlap with Master’s eligibility in some cases).  

---

### **PhD Scholarships**
1. **General PhD Scholarships**  
   - Cover tuition, registration fees, accommodation, and a living allowance at AIT’s residential campus for the full 41-month (7-semester) duration.  
   - The non-binding scholarship value is approximately **1.96 million baht** per student.  

2. **Research Fellow Program for Public Policy and Asian Study**  
   - Specifically designed for PhD students, focusing on research in public policy and Asian studies.  

---

### **Key Eligibility Criteria**
- **Master’s**: Strong academic records (GPA ≥ 3.5 or equivalent), English proficiency (IELTS 6.0 or AIT EET ≥ 6.0), and relevant field of study.  
- **PhD**: Equivalent academic requirements, research proposal, and English proficiency.  

For detailed application processes and specific program requirements, refer to AIT’s official scholarship guidelines.

column1: Does AIT offer assistantships, fellowships, or on-campus work opportunities as financial support?
column2:
AIT offers **assistantships**, **scholarships**, and **on-campus work opportunities** as forms of financial support. Here's a concise breakdown:

1. **Student Assistantships**:  
   - Available as academic employment, requiring application and approval based on academic excellence and faculty referrals.  
   - Students perform tasks for schools, faculty, or departments and receive payment.  
   - Aim to provide practical experience, deepen academic understanding, and build professional networks.  
   - **Website**: [Student Assistantships](https://ait.ac.th/student/student-assistantships/).

2. **Scholarships**:  
   - AIT offers scholarships for Master’s and Doctoral programs, covering part of tuition fees for qualified students.  
   - Additional financial support includes the **Asian Development Bank-Japan Scholarship Program (ADB-JSP)**, which covers expenses like proficiency courses and travel (but not personal expenses or conferences).  
   - Scholarships are limited and awarded based on competitive evaluation.  
   - **Website**: [Scholarships](https://ait.ac.th/financial/ait-scholarships/).

3. **On-Campus Work**:  
   - Assistantships are the primary on-campus work opportunity tied to financial support.  

**Note**: Internship programs are mentioned under career development but are not explicitly tied to financial aid.  

For more details, visit [AIT Scholarships](https://ait.ac.th/financial/ait-scholarships/) or [Student Assistantships](https://ait.ac.th/student/student-assistantships/).

## **Student Assistantships**

AIT has a formal **Student Assistantship program** that provides both work experience and financial compensation.<cite doc="web_markdown.pdf" page="202"/>

### **What is a Student Assistantship?**

"A Student Assistant is a graduate student offered a specific form of academic employment, for which students must apply and be accepted based on **academic excellence and faculty referral**. Student assistants receive payment based on the tasks they perform for schools, faculty members, or departments/units."<cite doc="web_markdown.pdf" page="202"/>

### **Objective:**
"To provide opportunities to the students to gain practical field experience, deepen academic understanding, and to develop a valuable network of contacts to look to for references and advice post-graduation."<cite doc="web_markdown.pdf" page="202"/>

## **Four Categories of Assistantships**<cite doc="web_markdown.pdf" page="202"/>

### **1. Teaching Assistants**

**Responsibilities:**
- Support teaching laboratory courses
- Conduct tutorials and discussion sections
- Including bridging courses and English tutorials

**Qualifications:**
- Doctoral and master candidates with **GPA of at least 3.50**
- Teaching background
- Proficiency in English/good communication skills

**Salary:** **200-300 Baht per hour**

### **2. Non-Instructional Teaching Assistants**

**Responsibilities:**
- Aid in instructional functions of the Institute
- NOT involved in oral instruction or e-teaching

**Qualifications:**
- Master's students with **GPA of at least 3.00** OR
- Doctoral candidates with **GPA of at least 3.50**
- Specific skills required for work

**Salary:** **150-250 Baht per hour**

### **3. Research Assistants**

**Responsibilities:**
- Assist faculty and staff with research and data collection
- Work as researchers, technical writers, field assistants

**Qualifications:**
- Master's students enrolled for thesis with **GPA of at least 2.75** OR
- Doctoral students with **GPA of at least 3.50**

**Salary:** **150-250 Baht per hour**

### **4. Staff Assistants**

**Responsibilities:**
- Work in schools and non-school units such as:
  - Secretariat of school
  - Offices
  - Library
  - Registry
  - Admissions
  - Career center
  - Housing

**Qualifications:**
- Master students with **GPA of at least 3.00**
- Needed administrative skills

**Salary:** **7,500 Baht per month for 20 months**
- Working minimum of **50 hours per month**

## **How to Apply for Student Assistantships**<cite doc="web_markdown.pdf" page="202"/>

"Student assistantships are offered through the schools, departments, administration, and various centers of AIT. Application requirements for student assistantships vary by school and as well as by the nature of the task assigned. All Student Assistantship openings will be posted in the **Student Assistantship System (SAS)**, and interested students can apply online. You may also contact your advisor, faculty, and departments for specific academic or research opportunities, which will be also posted in the SAS."

## **Important Notes**

### **Academic Advisor Approval:**
"Before applying for a student assistantship, you are advised to seek your **Academic Advisor's feedback to ensure approval and credit eligibility**."<cite doc="web_markdown.pdf" page="203"/>

### **Benefits Beyond Money:**
"Student assistantship is a unique experience during graduate studies. It provides an excellent learning environment, exposing students to what it is like to be in the workforce while providing the added benefit of a financial reward."<cite doc="web_markdown.pdf" page="202"/>

### **RTG Fellowships**

The document mentions **"RTG Fellowships"** as part of AIT Scholarships:<cite doc="web_markdown.pdf" page="205"/>
- Deadline: June 10 (for August intake)
- Application deadline suggests these are competitive fellowships

### **Fellows of AIT (Research Positions)**<cite doc="web_markdown.pdf" page="207"/>

AIT also offers **fellowship positions** for advanced researchers:

**Post-Doctoral Fellow:**
- For candidates who have completed a doctoral degree from an institution recognized by AIT
- Use Institute research facilities, library, and recreational facilities
- May audit courses with instructor permission

**Research Fellow:**
- For candidates whose qualifications are equivalent to an AIT master's degree student
